The invention aims to provide a molding with an integrated electrode pattern in which a band-shaped second film can be securely fixed to the inner surface of a resin molded body. More specifically, the invention provides a structure capable of reliably holding the second film in an upright or standing state relative to the inner surface of the resin molded body, while ensuring stable electrical connection between an electrode pattern formed on a first film and an external substrate.

The molding includes a resin molded body, a first film provided on an inner surface of the resin molded body, and a band-shaped second film arranged so as to stand on the inner surface of the resin molded body. The resin molded body may be formed by injection molding or another suitable resin molding process, and may constitute, for example, a housing, cover, panel, or other molded component in which an electrode pattern is integrated.

The first film is formed along the inner surface of the resin molded body. The first film includes an electrode pattern and a first lead-out wire electrically connected to the electrode pattern. The electrode pattern may function as, for example, a sensor electrode, antenna electrode, switch electrode, touch input electrode, or other conductive functional pattern. The first lead-out wire serves to draw out an electrical signal from the electrode pattern toward a connection region where electrical connection with another wiring member is established.

The second film is formed in a band shape and is disposed so as to extend away from, or stand on, the inner surface of the resin molded body. The second film includes a second lead-out wire that is electrically connected to the first lead-out wire of the first film. In addition, the second film has an electric connecting portion configured to be connected to an external substrate, such as a printed circuit board, flexible printed circuit board, control board, or other external electrical component. Through this configuration, the electrode pattern provided on the first film can be electrically connected to the external substrate via the first lead-out wire and the second lead-out wire.

In order to secure the second film to the resin molded body, the resin molded body includes a pair of support wall portions. These support wall portions are arranged so as to clamp both ends of a base part of the second film. The base part of the second film is a portion positioned near the inner surface of the resin molded body, where the second film rises from the molded body. By holding both ends of this base part between the pair of support wall portions, the second film is mechanically supported and prevented from falling over, shifting, peeling, or being displaced during handling, assembly, or connection to the external substrate.

Accordingly, the molding with an integrated electrode pattern can maintain a reliable electrical connection path from the electrode pattern to the external substrate, while also improving the mounting stability of the band-shaped second film. The pair of support wall portions formed in the resin molded body enables the second film to be firmly fixed without requiring a complicated additional fixing member, thereby improving assembly reliability and reducing the likelihood of connection failure.
outputs.L4:
A molding with an integrated electrode pattern and a method for manufacturing the same are provided. The molding includes a resin molded body having an inner surface on which an electrode pattern is formed, and a band-shaped second film provided with an external electrical connection portion. The second film is arranged so as to stand upright from the inner surface of the resin molded body, and its base portion is securely fixed to the molded body. This configuration enables the external electrical connection portion of the second film to be electrically connected to the electrode pattern while maintaining stable mechanical positioning.

In the proposed structure, a pair of support walls is formed integrally with the resin molded body. These support walls are disposed on both sides of the base portion of the second film and clamp or sandwich the second film between them. By holding the base of the second film in this manner, the support walls prevent displacement, tilting, peeling, or detachment of the film from the inner surface of the resin molded body. As a result, the second film can be maintained in a predetermined standing posture, and the electrical connection between the second film and the electrode pattern can be kept reliable over time.

The electrode pattern may be formed on a first film that is integrated with the resin molded body, or may be provided directly on the inner surface of the molded body. The second film is positioned so that a connection region thereof overlaps or contacts a corresponding terminal portion of the electrode pattern. Conductive bonding material, pressure contact, solder, anisotropic conductive film, or another suitable electrical connection means may be used to establish electrical continuity between the electrode pattern and the external electrical connection portion of the second film.

In manufacturing the molding, the second film is first positioned in a mold so that its base portion is located at a predetermined position corresponding to the inner surface of the molded body. Resin is then injected into the mold. During molding, the resin forms the molded body and also forms the paired support walls integrally with the molded body. The support walls are molded around or adjacent to the base portion of the second film, thereby fixing the second film in place as part of the molding process. After the resin has solidified, the second film remains clamped between the support walls and stands from the inner surface of the molded body.

Because the paired support walls are formed simultaneously with the resin molded body, no separate fixing member or additional assembly step is required. The support walls increase the holding strength of the second film and reduce stress applied to the electrical connection portion. This is particularly advantageous when the second film is used as a flexible wiring member, connector tail, antenna connection member, sensor connection member, or other external electrical connection component that may be subjected to bending, pulling, vibration, or repeated handling.

Accordingly, the molding with an integrated electrode pattern provides both improved electrical reliability and improved structural fixation. The second film can be accurately positioned, firmly retained, and reliably connected to the electrode pattern on the resin molded body. The manufacturing method also enables efficient production of such a structure by integrating the fixation of the second film with the resin molding process.

counterfactuals.output: A resin molded body includes a resin body having an inner surface, an electrode pattern integrated with the resin body, and a band-shaped second film electrically connected to the electrode pattern. The second film includes an external connection portion for connection to an external circuit and is disposed so as to stand upright from the inner surface of the resin body. counterfactuals.prompt: Write a Japanese-style patent abstract in English with sections labeled [Object] and [Solution] for an invention involving a molding with an integrated electrode pattern, a first film carrying electrodes and lead-out wires, and a second band-shaped film clamped by integral resin support walls.
counterfactuals.output:
[Object]  
To provide a molded article having an integrated electrode pattern in which electrodes and lead-out wires can be reliably positioned and protected within a molding, while improving connection reliability, reducing assembly steps, and preventing displacement or peeling of a film carrying the electrode pattern.

[Solution]  
A molding with an integrated electrode pattern includes a molded resin body, a first film provided with a plurality of electrodes and lead-out wires connected to the electrodes, and a second film formed in a band shape. The first film is integrated with the molded resin body so that the electrodes are disposed at predetermined positions on or in the molded resin body and the lead-out wires extend from the electrodes toward a connection portion. The molded resin body is formed with a pair of resin support walls integrally projecting therefrom. The second film is arranged along the lead-out wires and is clamped between the pair of resin support walls, thereby holding the first film and/or the lead-out wires in a prescribed position. By integrally forming the support walls with the molded resin body and retaining the band-shaped second film between the support walls, the electrode pattern is stably fixed to the molding, deformation and positional deviation of the lead-out wires are suppressed, and a highly reliable molded component having an integrated electrode structure is obtained.

This configuration enables reliable electrical connection to the inner electrode while maintaining the flexible film in a stable upright position, improving assembly reliability and durability of the molded resin component.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create the [Object] and [Solution] text for a patent about manufacturing a resin molded body containing an integrated electrode pattern, including a first film on the inner surface and a band-shaped second film supported at its base by paired wall portions.
counterfactuals.output:
[Object]  
To provide a method for manufacturing a resin molded body having an integrated electrode pattern, in which an electrode pattern can be accurately formed on a desired inner surface while maintaining the positional stability and shape of a film member during molding, particularly when a band-shaped film portion is arranged so as to project from or extend along the molded body.

[Solution]  
A method for manufacturing a resin molded body containing an integrated electrode pattern includes arranging, in a mold cavity, a first film having an electrode pattern formed thereon so that the first film is disposed along an inner surface of the resin molded body to be formed, and arranging a band-shaped second film connected to or continuous with the first film. The second film is positioned such that a base portion thereof is supported between a pair of wall portions provided in the mold cavity or formed as part of the molded body. A molten resin is then injected into the mold cavity and solidified, whereby the first film is integrally molded on the inner surface of the resin molded body and the band-shaped second film is fixed at its base portion by the paired wall portions. As a result, displacement, floating, bending, or deformation of the second film during resin injection is suppressed, and the electrode pattern is reliably integrated with the resin molded body in a predetermined position.

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce an English patent abstract for an in-mold electronics structure where a resin molded body includes a first film with an electrode pattern and lead-out wire, plus a second film with a lead-out wire connected to an external substrate and held upright by molded support walls.
